article_content: A newly revealed memo shows President Obama's administration received warnings about implementation challenges for the Affordable Care Act years before HealthCare.gov's troubled 2013 launch. David Cutler, a healthcare policy expert from Obama's 2008 campaign team, sent a memo to White House National Economic Council director Larry Summers in May 2010 predicting 'catastrophic issues' with the planned rollout. The document, obtained by CBS News, stated: 'I do not believe the relevant members of the Administration understand the President's vision or have the capability to carry it out.' Technical contractors later echoed these concerns in a September 6, 2013 report to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, citing 'near certainty' of system failures due to inadequate testing protocols before the October 1 launch. Despite multiple warnings spanning three years, the administration proceeded with a rollout that experienced major technical failures persisting over a month.

David Cutler, stručnjak za zdravstvenu politiku iz Obamine predizborne ekipe 2008., poslao je u maju 2010. memorandum Larryju Summersu, tadašnjem direktoru Nacionalnog ekonomskog savjeta Bijele kuće, upozoravajući na 'katastrofalne probleme' pri planiranom pokretanju sustava. Dokument objavljen na CBS News navodi: 'Smatram da relevantni članovi administracije ne razumiju predsjednikovu viziju niti imaju sposobnost da je provedu.' Tehnički izvođači su kasnije, u izvještaju za Centar za Medicare i Medicaid od 6. septembra 2013., ponovili ove zabrinutosti, upozoravajući na 'gotovo sigurne' sistemske probleme usljed nedovoljnih testova prije službenog pokretanja 1. oktobra. article_content: Survivors who escaped Auschwitz's gas chambers shared harrowing accounts 70 years after the camp's liberation by Soviet troops. Sam Pivnik recounted how he survived by prostrating himself before Dr. Josef Mengele, the camp's notorious physician. At 14, Pivnik was separated from his family in Bedzin, Poland, and endured imprisonment. 'Mengele pointed left - the death sentence - but I begged at his boots and was spared,' he recalled. Over 1.1 million people were systematically murdered at Auschwitz's network of camps through gas chambers, forced labor, and medical experiments. Edith Baneth described arriving to 'mountains of corpses,' while Susan Pollock survived with typhoid and severe malnutrition. Soviet soldiers liberated fewer than 8,000 remaining prisoners in January 1945 after Nazi forces abandoned partial destruction of the facilities. Survivors emphasize preserving memory through education and family bonds.

Sam Pivnik ispričao je kako je preživio bacivši se pred dr. Josefom Mengeleom, zloglasnim logorskim liječnikom. Kao 14-godišnjak, Pivnik je odvojen od porodice u Bedzinu (Poljska) i pretrpio je mjesece zatočeništva. 'Mengele je pokazao lijevo - smrtna presuda - ali sam se molio pred njegovim čizmama i pošteđen sam,' prisjetio se. article_content: Filmmaker Meghna Gulzar stated on Tuesday that creating 'Sam Bahadur', the upcoming biographical drama about Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw, proved transformative for her. Gulzar, known for films like 'Talvar' (2002) and 'Raazi' (2018), reunites with actor Vicky Kaushal to portray one of India's most celebrated military leaders. The trailer launched at New Delhi's Manekshaw Centre attended by Army Chief General Manoj Pande, co-stars Sanya Malhotra, Fatima Sana Shaikh, and producer Ronnie Screwvala. Gulzar emphasized the timeless relevance of Manekshaw's values: 'Living with truth and integrity never goes out of style. His story deserves to reach all generations.' Reflecting on the project, she added: 'This experience fundamentally changed me. If audiences feel even a fraction of his impact, we've succeeded - they truly don't make leaders like him anymore.' The film spans Manekshaw's 40-year career (1934-1973), including World War II service and leadership during the 1971 Indo-Pakistani War that led to Bangladesh's independence. Gulzar acknowledged the challenge of condensing decades into a feature: 'We prioritized key events while weaving in personal moments. Capturing his spirit mattered more than just physical resemblance.' Kaushal, Gulzar's first choice after their successful 'Raazi' collaboration, committed immediately without reading the script. The team focused on authentic portrayal through mannerisms rather than prosthetics. 'Our shared understanding deepened - now we communicate almost wordlessly,' Gulzar noted about their creative partnership. Produced by RSVP Movies, the December 1 release features Malhotra as Manekshaw's wife Silloo and Shaikh as former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. The screenplay was co-written by Bhavani Iyer, Shantanu Shrivastava, and Gulzar.

Gulzar, poznata po ostvarenjima poput 'Talvar' (2002) i 'Raazi' (2018), ponovo je okupila tim sa glumcem Vickyjem Kaushalom kako bi predstavila priču o jednom od najuglednijih vojnih ličnosti Indije. Gulzar je istakla trajnu vrijednost Manekshawovih principa: 'Život proveden u poštivanju istine i časti nikad neće izaći iz mode. Njegova biografija treba da bude dostupna svim generacijama.' Dodala je: 'Ovaj projekt temeljito me promijenio. Ako publika prepozna makar djelić njegove veličine, smatrat ćemo da smo uspjeli - takve vođe više ne postoje.' Kaushal je bez oklevanja prihvatio ulogu nakon uspješne saradnje na filmu 'Raazi'. Tim je odbio upotrebu šminke za starenje, fokusirajući se na autentičnost pokreta. 'Sada se razumijemo bez riječi - saradnja teče prirodno,' izjavila je Gulzar o kreativnom partnerstvu. Film 'Sam Bahadur' kompanije RSVP Movies, sa Malhotrom kao Manekshawovom suprugom i Shaikh u ulozi Indire Gandhi, premijerno će biti prikazan 1. decembra. Scenarij potpisuju Bhavani Iyer, Shantanu Shrivastava i sama Gulzar.

article_content: A new time-lapse video captures New York City's dynamic energy from a cyclist's perspective. The four-minute film follows blogger Michael Green on a 12-mile journey through Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn, traversing the Brooklyn, Manhattan, and Williamsburg bridges. Using a helmet-mounted camera, Green passes historic landmarks including City Hall, the 1883-opened Brooklyn Bridge, and Borough Hall, concluding at the Brooklyn Bridge waterfront. Produced in partnership with Virgin Atlantic and urban guide Nick Reale, the project highlights NYC's cycling infrastructure development, including over 30 miles of protected bike lanes created since 2007 to enhance rider safety and promote tourism.

article_content: Emerging research indicates tablets are transforming digital engagement patterns, with iPads showing distinctive evening usage peaks. Data analysis reveals most intensive tablet activity occurs between 7 PM and 11 PM - coinciding with traditional television prime-time hours. This suggests users might either multitask with multiple screens or prioritize tablet use over TV programming. The ReadItLater study, leveraging timestamped content-saving data, highlights contrasting device usage patterns. Desktop computers maintain steady daytime engagement aligned with work hours, while smartphones exhibit brief spikes matching typical commute schedules. iPads break this mold with prolonged evening usage, mirroring historical patterns of post-dinner reading rituals adapted for digital formats. Media strategists observe significant implications for advertising models predicated on undivided TV attention. This behavioral shift aligns with new digital publications like Rupert Murdoch's Daily and expanding Android tablet adoption. The trend challenges conventional media consumption assumptions, suggesting evolving user preferences for portable, on-demand content during leisure hours.

article_content: A Chinese family has welcomed a newborn son, Bei Bei, in a bid to save their three-year-old daughter Pan Jing from acute leukemia. Born on May 31, 2024, at Changji Hospital in China's Xinjiang Autonomous Region, Bei Bei's cord blood will be used for a stem cell transplant recommended by doctors. Parents Zhao Linjun and Pan Qilong pursued this option after Jing's diagnosis in early 2023. The treatment costs approximately ¥500,000 (£50,000), posing financial challenges. Cord blood—containing embryonic stem cells—is used in bone-marrow transplants for leukemia. While promising, the procedure carries risks, as seen in a 2023 case where Rob and Cindy Harris conceived via IVF to obtain cord blood for their son with Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome. Pan Qilong stated, 'I must save my daughter,' while fundraising. Medical experts confirm cord blood transplants are less invasive than traditional methods but still involve potential complications.

article_content: Phoenix (CNN) – Alex Teves cherished Marvel and DC comics, finding inspiration in Spider-Man and Batman. His high school English teachers noted his insightful analyses of superhero themes exploring good versus evil. The 24-year-old, who died shielding his girlfriend during the 2012 Aurora theater shooting, is remembered by his Phoenix community as an exemplar of kindness and purpose. 'Alex wasn't exceptional in any typical way – he was exceptional in how he cared,' says his father Tom Teves. The Teves family now leads a campaign called the Alex Teves Challenge, urging media outlets to stop publishing mass shooters' names and images, arguing this coverage inspires copycat attacks. After earning a master's in psychological counseling from the University of Denver, Alex planned to pursue physical therapy to 'heal whole persons,' according to family. His former teachers describe a conscientious student who brought humor and positivity to classrooms at Desert Vista High School, where peers once held 'Alex Teves Day' to honor his signature style and inclusive nature. Tom Teves condemns media coverage focusing on the Aurora shooter: 'These killers want fame. When we plaster their faces everywhere, we're giving them what they want.' The family's crusade has gained support nationwide, with memorial events encouraging attendees to emulate Alex's casual attire as a tribute. The article contrasts Alex's legacy of compassion with the shooter's infamy, noting the perpetrator's neuroscience studies at University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus and mental health history. 'Alex would've tried to help someone like him,' says school principal Anna Battle. 'That's the tragedy – we lost someone who could've made a difference.'

article_content: NBA Hall of Famer Dennis Rodman and several former basketball stars arrived in North Korea to participate in a goodwill basketball game celebrating leader Kim Jong-Un's 31st birthday on January 8. The event comes three weeks after North Korea's December 2013 execution of Kim's uncle Jang Song Thaek. Rodman's delegation includes NBA veterans Kenny Anderson, Cliff Robinson, Vin Baker, Craig Hodges, Doug Christie, and Charles D. Smith. While Rodman emphasized sports diplomacy and personal rapport with Kim Jong-Un, the U.S. State Department reiterated concerns about North Korea's human rights record. This marks Rodman's fourth visit since February 2013, when he first met Kim during an exhibition game featuring Harlem Globetrotters. Despite recent political tensions and Paddy Power's sponsorship withdrawal, Rodman's team maintains the visit focuses purely on basketball. South Korean athletes offered mixed perspectives, with 1991 table tennis champion Hyun Jung-Wha praising sports diplomacy efforts while 1999 basketball player Cho Sung-Won questioned Rodman's motives. Former NBA player Vin Baker stated: 'This is strictly about the game and love for basketball.' The visit continues to spark international debate about using sports as diplomatic tools in politically sensitive contexts.

article_content: (CNN) -- The anticipation for 'The Dark Knight Rises' has reached unprecedented levels, with tickets selling out months before its July 20, 2012 U.S. premiere. Early reviews now circulating suggest the film meets sky-high expectations. The Hollywood Reporter's Todd McCarthy calls it 'big-time Hollywood filmmaking at its most accomplished,' noting it makes Marvel films appear 'silly and childish.' While acknowledging it lacks Heath Ledger's iconic Joker performance from 'The Dark Knight,' McCarthy praises it as the trilogy's strongest entry. Set eight years after previous events, the story finds Bruce Wayne in isolation as Gotham City blames Batman for District Attorney Harvey Dent's death. Tom Hardy's Bane disrupts the city's fragile peace, forcing Batman out of retirement with help from Anne Hathaway's Selina Kyle. Critics highlight the film's exploration of economic inequality and social unrest, with Variety's Justin Chang noting its 'seething vision of urban anxiety' addressing wealth disparity and systemic neglect. Reviewers universally praise the film's ambition, with Time's Richard Corliss declaring it 'the best, most troubling, assured and enthralling of all superhero movies,' even if it might not match 'The Avengers' box office success.

article_content: The search for extraterrestrial life currently focuses on three primary avenues: detecting microbial life within our solar system, identifying technosignatures from intelligent civilizations, or observing biosignatures in exoplanet atmospheres. Dr. Susan Schneider, a philosophy professor at the University of Connecticut, hypothesizes that advanced extraterrestrial civilizations might exist as artificial intelligence rather than biological entities. This perspective parallels humanity's increasing integration with technology, suggesting a potential evolutionary trajectory toward post-biological existence. In collaboration with SETI astronomer Dr. Seth Shostak, Schneider posits that silicon-based intelligence could overcome biological limitations, stating: 'Our cerebral capacity is constrained by cranial dimensions, whereas artificial systems could operate at planetary scales.' This theory resonates with Professor Stephen Hawking's cautions regarding AI's existential risks, though he concurrently acknowledged its capacity to address global challenges. Recent proceedings from the Library of Congress' Astrobiology Symposium emphasized divergent astrobiological approaches. While microbial life detection remains the most plausible near-term achievement through Martian exploration or exoplanet atmospheric analysis via instruments like the James Webb Space Telescope (deployed in 2021), encountering advanced machine intelligence would present unprecedented philosophical and societal challenges. A University of Cádiz survey assessing public readiness for extraterrestrial contact revealed significant knowledge gaps, with 18% of respondents unaware of the 1969 Moon landing. SETI researchers estimate a 20-year horizon for potential microbial discovery, while continuous monitoring of cosmic radio signals persists through initiatives like the Allen Telescope Array.

article_content: (CNN) -- A passenger injured during the emergency evacuation of Southwest Airlines Flight 345 has filed a lawsuit, her attorney confirmed. The Boeing 737 experienced a nose gear collapse upon landing at New York's LaGuardia Airport on July 22. Jacqueline Young, 48, sustained injuries to multiple body parts during the slide evacuation process, according to legal representative Sanford Rubenstein. Official reports indicate 10 minor injuries among the 150 passengers onboard. The aircraft came to rest with its nose on the runway before diverting into adjacent grass. National Transportation Safety Board analysis revealed the nose gear touched down before main wheels, deviating from standard landing protocols. While initial FAA communications mentioned possible pre-landing concerns, later review of air traffic control records showed no prior mechanical alerts. Southwest Airlines declined to comment citing pending litigation.

article_content: An innovative eco-friendly cottage on Denmark's Laesoe Island features roofing and wall materials made entirely from seaweed. Architects utilized over eight tons of eelgrass—harvested from nearby waters using excavators, then stored on marshes for natural rainwater cleansing before sun-drying. The compressed seaweed bales form walls and a 1-meter-thick roof. Designed by Copenhagen architect Soren Nielsen, the 100-square-meter house took four months to construct. It features a central living-dining area, open kitchen, two attic spaces, and south-facing terraces with outdoor bathing facilities. Nielsen stated: 'This project demonstrates how overlooked organic materials can be integrated into modern low-carbon construction.' The unique property is listed at £350,000 (equivalent to 3.2 million DKK in 2013).

Sabijeni balevi formiraju zidove i krov debljine jednog metra. Projekt je dizajnirao kopenhagenski arhitekt Soren Nielsen. Kuća od 100 kvadratnih metara izgrađena je za četiri mjeseca te uključuje centralni dnevni boravak s otvorenom kuhinjom, dva potkrovna prostora i južno orijentirane terase sa vanjskim kupatilom. article_content: On a historic evening at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium, Glenn Maxwell delivered one of cricket's greatest ODI performances, powering Australia to a dramatic three-wicket victory over Afghanistan and securing their World Cup semifinal berth against South Africa. Facing near-certain defeat at 91/7 while chasing 292, Maxwell (201* off 128 balls) partnered with captain Pat Cummins in a record 202-run eighth-wicket stand, overcoming severe cramps to complete the highest successful run chase in World Cup history. The match drew parallels to Kapil Dev's legendary 175* against Zimbabwe in 1983, with Australian players maintaining superstitious dressing room positions during Maxwell's innings. Josh Hazlewood later described the knock as 'the No.1 ODI innings ever witnessed,' highlighting Maxwell's 360-degree shot-making that left opponents strategizing helplessly. Despite Afghanistan posting their highest World Cup total (291/5) through late-innings acceleration, Maxwell's heroics secured Australia's progression to the semifinals.

Događaj podsjeća na Kapil Devovu legendarnu inningsu od 175* protiv Zimbabvea 1983., pri čemu su Australci praznovjerno ostajali na svojim mjestima u svlačionici tijekom Maxwellovog napada. article_content: Recent reports from South Korean media have intensified speculation about North Korean leader Kim Jong Il's health status. North Korea's state media continues to dismiss foreign health reports as exaggerated speculation.

article_content: By Steve Keating, Reuters French player Jo-Wilfried Tsonga continued his impressive run at the Rogers Cup, defeating Bulgaria's Grigor Dimitrov 6-4, 6-3 on Saturday to advance to the final of the Canadian hardcourt tournament. After victories over world number one Novak Djokovic in the third round and two-time champion Andy Murray in the quarterfinals, the 13th-seeded Tsonga overcame seventh-seeded Dimitrov in sweltering conditions to reach his second final this season. Tsonga will face 20-time Grand Slam champion Roger Federer, a two-time Canadian Open winner, in the championship match. 'I've waited years for this moment,' said Tsonga, who has reached three semifinals in four Canadian appearances but only one previous final. 'This validates my perseverance and gives me motivation to keep pushing,' added the Frenchman, whose aggressive style draws comparisons to boxing legend Muhammad Ali. Dimitrov, ranked among tennis's rising stars with three 2014 titles, acknowledged the defeat: 'Tsonga played well, but I didn't elevate my game as needed. Still, I'll focus on the positives heading into the U.S. Open.'

article_content: The use of lethal injection as a form of capital punishment is becoming increasingly rare worldwide, with the European Union prohibiting it for member states. Texas continues to maintain high execution rates, having carried out 578 executions as of July 2024. Kimberly McCarthy, an African-American woman convicted of a 1997 murder, faced execution amid ongoing debates about racial disparities in capital punishment. Historical context reveals how marginalized groups—from 19th-century Irish immigrants to modern disadvantaged communities—face disproportionate criminalization. Analysis suggests poverty and systemic neglect drive these patterns more than inherent criminality, with Denmark's social welfare model presented as an alternative approach. The 1924 resignation of Warden R.F. Coleman over execution duties contrasts with current practices. The article advocates addressing root causes through societal support to reduce both crime and reliance on capital punishment, referencing 144 national death row exonerations since 1973.

article_content: Scalpers are capitalizing on unprecedented demand for the new iPhone 6 by reselling pre-ordered devices at significantly inflated prices. Pre-orders launched in Australia last Friday overwhelmed Apple's systems, causing website crashes. Numerous eBay listings now show iPhone 6 Plus models priced as high as $2,999 – over $1,600 above Apple's official $1,129 price for the 64GB model. Consumer advocate Tom Godfrey from Choice warned buyers against paying premium prices, noting that first-generation devices often contain technical issues. 'Apple conducted a synchronized global release, so waiting ensures better availability and avoids initial bugs,' Godfrey told the Sydney Morning Herald. He suggested considering alternatives like the Samsung Galaxy S5 or HTC One M8, which offer competitive features at lower prices. The iPhone 6 series ranges from $869 for the base model to $1,249 for the top-tier configuration, available in three storage capacities (16GB, 64GB, 128GB) and multiple finishes.

article_content: Classic rocker Bob Geldof joined the star-studded lineup at Poland's EnergaCamerimage Film Festival, introducing a screening of the 1982 musical drama 'Pink Floyd - The Wall.' He appeared alongside the film's cinematographer Peter Biziou, this year's lifetime achievement honoree. When asked if director Alan Parker's work represented a career peak, Geldof responded bluntly: 'No, I don't like the film. I think I'm really bad.' 'I watched it twice and cringed,' Geldof confessed, praising Biziou's supportive presence during filming. 'I can't stand seeing or hearing myself - especially not giant projections.' Regarding his initial motivation for taking the role, Geldof quipped: 'Money,' while humorously blaming Pink Floyd's 'hippie-era accounting' for modest compensation. The Boomtown Rats frontman dismissed rock musicians' acting abilities: 'Bowie? Not good. Sting? Not good. Me? Definitely not.' He contrasted this with Elvis Presley and Frank Sinatra's screen success: 'They interpreted songs rather than writing them. That psychological distance helps acting.' Declaring modern music stagnant, Geldof stated: 'Rock's last giants were Nirvana and Oasis. Hip-hop's golden age ended with NWA and Eminem. Now it's all reruns, barring Kanye's brilliance.' Addressing humanitarian efforts, he emphasized daily Band-Aid Trust work and linked poverty reduction to conflict prevention: 'Feed people, fund peace.' Teasing future projects, Geldof revealed plans for a Live Aid Imax film, Disney+ documentary series, and 'Just For One Day' musical debuting January 2024 at London's Old Vic. The Camerimage festival runs through November 18.

article_content: When facing a 1-0 deficit with limited time remaining, managers face critical decisions about star players. This dilemma recently confronted both current Manchester United coach Louis van Gaal and his predecessor David Moyes regarding striker Robin van Persie. Their contrasting approaches produced opposite results. In December 2013, Moyes opted to keep an underperforming Van Persie on the field during Manchester United's 1-0 loss to Newcastle, later citing fear of fan criticism. 'Substituting our top scorer while trailing might have drawn backlash,' Moyes explained post-match. Meanwhile, Van Gaal made the bold move to substitute Van Persie during Netherlands' 2014 World Cup match against Mexico with 14 minutes remaining. The replacement player Klaas-Jan Huntelaar contributed directly to both goals in their 2-1 victory, assisting Wesley Sneijder's equalizer before scoring the decisive penalty. Van Gaal's strategic substitutions proved decisive throughout the tournament, with reserve players Memphis Depay and Leroy Fer making crucial impacts in previous matches against Australia and Chile respectively. Analysts highlight this proactive approach as characteristic of Van Gaal's leadership style, contrasting sharply with Moyes' more cautious tactics during his United tenure.

article_content: Three NHS surgeons have been prohibited from performing laparoscopic upper gastrointestinal cancer surgeries following patient fatalities, according to official reports. Legal teams are examining 17 additional cases involving potential surgical complications. The surgeons remain employed by Maidstone and Tunbridge Wells NHS Trust in Kent but are restricted to general surgical duties. A Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) investigation (2012-2013) identified 'potentially avoidable outcomes' and questioned clinical decision-making standards. Five deaths have been directly linked to these procedures, with bereaved families pursuing legal action. The hospital trust faces criticism for not disclosing the complete RCS report and continuing the surgeons' employment. Notable cases include a 51-year-old patient who died during corrective surgery and Philip Coleman, 63, whose widow demanded accountability. The General Medical Council is assessing the surgeons' professional standing. Trust representatives confirmed implementing RCS recommendations to halt laparoscopic GI cancer operations but asserted no evidence supports broader restrictions on the surgeons' general practice.

article_content: (CNN) -- The head of a UN nuclear watchdog group stated Friday that a deal with Iran over its nuclear program is likely in January 2023. This agreement would allow inspectors to access the Parchin military complex where nuclear material testing is suspected. The announcement followed reports that the International Atomic Energy Agency concluded one-day talks in Iran regarding its nuclear program, which Western nations suspect serves as cover for weapons development - allegations Iran consistently denies. 'We've agreed to meet again on 16 January next year to finalize the structured approach and begin implementation shortly afterward,' IAEA chief inspector Herman Nackaerts told reporters in Vienna. Access to Parchin remains crucial, though not yet granted: 'It's part of the structured approach we hope to implement soon,' Nackaerts added. Iran's IAEA representative Ali Asghar Soltanieh described the talks as constructive in state media reports, without confirming discussions about Parchin access. The next round of negotiations is scheduled for January 16. Meanwhile, the US imposed new sanctions Thursday targeting Iranian companies and individuals allegedly supporting nuclear development, including Prof. Fereydoun Abbasi Davani - head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization who survived a 2010 assassination attempt. The sanctions freeze US assets and prohibit business dealings. US officials cited Iran's 'continued intransigence' as justification. While Iran maintains its nuclear program is purely for energy, the IAEA states it cannot verify peaceful intentions. Western sanctions have targeted Iran's economy and nuclear capabilities since 2010, including recent oil embargoes and banking restrictions.

article_content: (CNN) -- Five suspected pirates went on trial Tuesday in the Netherlands in what authorities describe as Europe's first piracy trial. The case against the Somali men began at Rotterdam District Court and is expected to last five days, according to Wim de Bruin, spokesperson for the Dutch National Prosecutor's Office. The defendants were apprehended by the Dutch Navy in January 2009 during an anti-piracy operation in the Gulf of Aden after an attack on a Dutch Antilles-flagged cargo ship. De Bruin stated: 'The pirates' vessel was disabled by the Danish Navy, leading to their capture and transfer to Dutch authorities. They face charges of maritime robbery, with potential sentences of 9-12 years if convicted.' The accused are identified as Ahmed Yusuf Farah (25), Jama Mohamed Samatar (45), Abdirisaq Abdulahi Hirsi (33), Sayid Ali Garaar (39), and Osman Musse Farah (32). Separately, Somali national Abduwali Abdukhadir Muse awaits sentencing in the U.S. after pleading guilty to hijacking the Maersk Alabama in April 2009. Muse, who faces up to 34 years imprisonment, admitted to charges including hostage-taking during his May 19 court appearance in New York. The Dutch defendants remained aboard a Danish naval ship for four weeks post-capture before transfer to the Netherlands. Prosecutors gathered testimony from Danish Navy personnel and crew members of the targeted cargo ship during pre-trial proceedings. Five Dutch defense attorneys represent the suspects, though their pleas remain unconfirmed. Concurrently, Germany prepares to try 10 piracy suspects captured in a separate Gulf of Aden incident involving a German vessel. These individuals, initially detained by Dutch authorities, were extradited to Germany following a formal request two months ago. CNN's Eileen Hsieh contributed reporting.

article_content: Washington (CNN) – President Barack Obama has responded to critiques from his former national security officials regarding Syria policy decisions. In a recent CBS '60 Minutes' interview aired Sunday, Obama defended his 2012 choice not to arm Syrian rebels fighting Bashar al-Assad's regime, stating it 'would have been counterproductive.' 'This addresses the myth that providing weapons two and a half years ago would have resolved Syria's crisis,' Obama remarked. 'Such action might have unnecessarily escalated U.S. involvement without improving the situation.' The President recently authorized airstrikes and rebel training specifically targeting ISIS, which has gained significant territory in both Syria and Iraq. This marks a strategic shift from his 2012 position. Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and ex-Defense Secretary Leon Panetta have publicly disagreed with Obama's earlier approach. Clinton's 2014 memoir 'Hard Choices' details her advocacy for arming rebels in 2012, arguing that inaction allowed jihadist groups to fill the power vacuum. At last week's Clinton Global Initiative meeting, Clinton declined to directly address whether rebel support came too late but acknowledged ISIS as a regional threat. She stated: 'While hypotheticals remain unproven, current realities demand immediate action.' Both Clinton and Panetta now endorse the current anti-ISIS operations.

article_content: How's your sitting position right now? That rounded upper back might resemble a fantasy creature's silhouette more than a healthy human posture. Medical experts warn this could be harming your cognitive functions. Dr Aishwarya Ahliwale from SRV Hospitals' physiotherapy department notes that slouching increases muscle tension and restricts blood circulation to the brain, potentially impairing mental performance. Colleague Dr K V Shivanand Reddy, a neurosurgeon at CARE Hospitals, emphasizes that poor alignment affects both self-confidence and social perceptions, creating psychological stress that compounds physical strain. Maintaining proper posture enhances oxygen intake and reduces neck/back pressure, which researchers associate with better neurological function. While the exact mechanisms remain under study, both doctors stress that regular exercise and ergonomic adjustments significantly contribute to brain health preservation. Recovery prospects depend on condition severity and timeline, with physical therapy and mindful posture practices being primary solutions. Severe cases might require surgical intervention, though complete reversal of chronic damage isn't guaranteed. 'Consistent effort and early action are crucial for optimal outcomes,' advises Dr Ahliwale.

article_content: By Ruth Styles | Updated: 14:03 EST, 26 March 2013 New motherhood brings sleepless nights, physical discomfort, and lifestyle changes - challenges amplified for Trish, 25, who parents without use of her arms or legs due to arthrogryposis. Despite assumptions she couldn't manage, Trish adapts using her teeth for tasks from meal preparation to diaper changes. 'You find ways to do everything,' says the mother of three from South Shields, including Jessica (4), PJ (2), and a newborn. Michelle, 26, faces similar challenges with pseudoachondroplasia (a rare form of dwarfism). Her 2-year-old Treziah nearly matches her 3ft 6in height, requiring safety reins outdoors. Both mothers emphasize creative problem-solving: 'Motherhood's harder but more rewarding than challenging,' Trish notes. Their stories feature in BBC Three's documentary 'A Special Kind of Mum' airing tonight at 9pm.

article_content: Shakira reached a last-minute settlement with Spanish prosecutors over tax evasion allegations on the opening day of her Barcelona trial. The 46-year-old Colombian singer (full name: Shakira Isabel Mebarak Ripoll) agreed Monday to pay a €7.3 million ($8 million) fine plus an additional €438,000 ($478,000) penalty, receiving a suspended three-year sentence. Prosecutors alleged she failed to pay €14.5 million ($15.8 million) in taxes from 2012-2014. Spanish law considers individuals residents for tax purposes after six months' residence. The case focused on Shakira's time in Spain during those years, despite her official address being listed in the Bahamas - a jurisdiction with lower tax rates. The singer was previously named in the 'Paradise Papers' leak exposing offshore financial activities. Prosecutors planned to call 117 witnesses regarding her residency, including beauty professionals, healthcare workers, and her driver. Had she been convicted, Shakira faced up to eight years and two months imprisonment plus a €23.8 million ($26 million) fine. Evidence included her 2012 Barcelona home purchase with ex-partner Gerard Piqué (a retired Spanish soccer player), where they lived with their two sons before separating in June 2022. Shakira's legal team argued her income primarily came from international tours during the disputed period. In a Monday statement, Shakira maintained innocence but cited family concerns: 'My lawyers were confident of victory, but I choose resolution for my children's sake.' She noted using PwC and EY tax advisors and criticized Spain's 'targeting' of celebrities. A second tax investigation remains pending, per Reuters. Spain continues enforcing tax reforms and offshore wealth tracking, having previously fined athletes Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi under similar circumstances. Both avoided jail through suspended sentences.

article_content: An investigation is underway at Royal Bolton Hospital following allegations that a patient died from uncontrolled bleeding while under care. Hospital administrators initiated a serious case review after a male patient's unexpected death in March on the High Dependency Ward. Bolton NHS Foundation Trust will lead the probe, with findings to be shared with trust leadership and NHS Bolton Clinical Commissioning Group. Hospital spokesperson Heather Edwards stated: 'We confirm an incident where a patient sadly died unexpectedly. A review panel will examine whether different actions could have prevented this outcome. The final report will be presented to our board, CCG, and the family upon completion. Police are not involved.' This follows a 2013 inquest into 86-year-old James Bent's death from blood loss after an antibiotic drip became detached unnoticed for two hours. Coroners ruled his death resulted from accidental equipment detachment compounded by pre-existing health conditions. article_content: At least thirteen people lost their lives in devastating mudslides triggered by Tropical Storm Fernand's impact on Mexico's eastern coastline, authorities reported Monday. Initially making landfall as a tropical storm Sunday evening, Fernand rapidly weakened into a depression before dissipating by Monday afternoon. Despite its diminishing strength, the system unleashed torrential rains across Veracruz state, resulting in lethal landslides that buried multiple residences. Governor Javier Duarte confirmed via Mexico's official Notimex news outlet that all casualties stemmed from these mud-related disasters. Meteorologists from the Miami-based National Hurricane Center noted Fernand's formation over the western Bay of Campeche, with residual storm activity located 75 miles west-southwest of Tuxpan at last measurement. The system dumped 4-8 inches of rainfall across five states, with localized areas receiving over 15 inches. Officials continue warning residents about potential additional landslides in vulnerable zones. CNN's Mexico affiliate contributed to this reporting.

article_content: The Supreme Court will soon rule on whether corporations must comply with the Affordable Care Act's requirement to provide contraceptive coverage without cost-sharing. While companies like Hobby Lobby and Conestoga Wood Specialties cite religious objections, the broader public health implications demand attention. Peer-reviewed research from the Contraceptive CHOICE Project (2007-2011) demonstrates that eliminating cost barriers enables 75% of women to choose highly effective long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) like IUDs and implants - compared to 12% national usage rates when out-of-pocket costs apply. As preventive healthcare, contraceptive access reduces ovarian/uterine cancer risks and manages menstrual health beyond pregnancy prevention. The ACA's mandate reflects medical consensus on these benefits. Our study of 9,000 participants showed that comprehensive access and education could prevent an estimated 72 unintended pregnancies per 1,000 women annually, suggesting significant potential to reduce abortion rates through policy implementation.

Kao dio preventivne zdravstvene zaštite, pristup kontracepciji smanjuje rizik od karcinoma jajnika i materice te reguliše menstrualne cikluse osim što sprečava neželjene trudnoće. article_content: Hong Kong (CNN) - China launched an anti-terrorism campaign one day after explosions at a Urumqi market killed dozens in Xinjiang, state news agency Xinhua reported Friday. Authorities initiated a 'one-year crackdown on violent terrorist activities' following attacks that killed 39 civilians and injured over 90. Five attackers were identified - four died in the blasts and one was arrested. Security checks intensified at border crossings, including inspections of individuals, vehicles, and postal deliveries. Public Security Minister Guo Shengkun and President Xi Jinping called for severe punishment of perpetrators. Witnesses described SUVs crashing into shoppers at 7:50 a.m. Thursday, with explosives thrown from vehicles before detonation. Social media images showed bodies amid burning wreckage. Many victims were elderly market regulars. The U.S. condemned the 'despicable act of violence.' Recent months saw increased security in Xinjiang following multiple attacks, including an April train station explosion that killed three. Analysts note a shift toward targeting civilians and spreading violence beyond Xinjiang. Ethnic tensions persist between Uyghurs and Han Chinese, with disputes over economic opportunities and security policies.

During her four-day trip, the pop star visited Mkoko Primary School where her organization funded classroom block construction. Malawian officials clarified these were additions to existing schools rather than new institutions. President Banda's office released a statement accusing Madonna of expecting VIP treatment and overstating her charity's impact. This followed Madonna's adoptions of David Banda (2006) and Mercy James (2009), whose biological families report limited contact despite initial agreements. Education Minister Eunice Kazembe stated: 'Ten classroom blocks were donated, not complete schools. While helpful, this represents a modest contribution.' Records show Madonna's charity donated $400,000 to BuildOn, an organization that has constructed schools in Malawi for 20 years. Controversy persists over the unbuilt £10 million girls' academy originally promised as part of adoption agreements. The government had waived 18-month residency requirements for international adoptions based on this pledge. Additional tensions stem from Madonna's 2011 dismissal of the president's sister from charity leadership following financial discrepancies. Madonna's spokesperson denied special treatment requests and highlighted educational contributions. Critics note her total £7 million donations since 2006 show limited impact given Malawi's development needs.

article_content: SAT scores among U.S. high school seniors show persistent stagnation, according to 2014 data from the College Board. Average scores remained unchanged at 497 in reading, 513 in math, and 487 in writing, with only 583 students achieving a perfect 2,400 score out of 1.7 million test-takers. The college readiness benchmark was met by 43% of students, mirroring recent trends. Significant racial disparities persist: 53% of white and 61% of Asian test-takers met the standard, compared to 16% of African-American, 24% of Hispanic, and 33% of Native American students. With SAT revisions scheduled for 2016, AP exam participation shows growth but reveals equity gaps. While 13.2% of public high school students passed at least one AP exam in 2014 - nearly double the rate from a decade prior - only 13% of African-American and 12% of Native American students participated. The College Board highlighted 'missed opportunities,' noting 40% of PSAT/NMSQT-identified candidates didn't take recommended AP courses.

Kriterij spremnosti za fakultetski nivo postiglo je 43% učenika, što odražava trendove posljednjih godina. article_content: The 2013 election of Argentine Cardinal Jorge Bergoglio as Pope Francis marked a watershed moment for global Catholicism, representing the first pontiff from Latin America in the Church's two-millennia history. This historic appointment resonated deeply with many Latino Catholics, including commentator Ruben Navarrette, who describes it as a long-overdue recognition of Latin America's central role in the faith. Navarrette, a self-described 'selective adherent' who attends Mass sporadically, articulates the complex relationship many modern Catholics maintain with their Church. While maintaining personal devotion, he criticizes institutional failures - particularly the clergy abuse scandals exemplified by the Los Angeles Archdiocese's $10 million legal settlement and Cardinal Roger Mahony's controversial legacy. The commentary highlights how cultural representation influences religious engagement, comparing papal excitement to political milestones like Mitt Romney's presidential bid. With Latin America's 480 million Catholics comprising nearly half the global total of 1.2 billion, the election symbolizes both regional pride and potential for renewed spiritual engagement among US Latinos (40-50 million members). Pope Francis' chosen name honoring St. Francis of Assisi signals priorities aligned with economic justice, while his Argentine background offers relatability to marginalized communities. The article concludes that this leadership shift positions Latin America - increasingly seen as Catholicism's demographic future - at the forefront of institutional evolution.

S obzirom da 480 miliona latinoameričkih katolika čini gotovo polovicu od 1,2 milijarde vjernika širom svijeta, papin izbor simbolizira i regionalni ponos te potencijal za obnovu duhovnog angažmana među 40-50 miliona američkih Latino katolika. article_content: (CNN) -- This wasn't how Stanislas Wawrinka envisioned his career trajectory. The unassuming Swiss tennis player hadn't anticipated defeating two of tennis' greatest champions to claim a Grand Slam title. Climbing to world No. 3 or surpassing Roger Federer as Switzerland's top-ranked player seemed improbable. That changed Sunday when Wawrinka defeated Rafael Nadal in four sets (6-3, 6-2, 3-6, 6-3) to win the Australian Open. 'I never dreamed of this situation - it's unbelievable,' the 28-year-old told CNN after overcoming the 13-time major champion. 'You keep reminding yourself: You just won a Grand Slam. It's incredible.' Wawrinka humorously verified his new top-four ranking via social media: 'Just checking!!!' he tweeted. The eighth seed dominated early sets before Nadal, competing with a back injury sustained during warm-ups, claimed the third set. Despite Nadal's resilience, Wawrinka maintained composure during crucial fourth-set moments, even employing self-motivation tactics like head-tapping to stay focused. 'I needed to control the pace and trust my serve,' Wawrinka explained. His strategic forehand ultimately secured victory, marking Switzerland's second male Grand Slam triumph alongside his 2008 Olympic doubles gold with Federer. 'The Olympic victory remains special - my first major win with a close friend for Switzerland,' Wawrinka reflected. 'But this Grand Slam title... it's indescribable.'

'Morao sam kontrolirati tempo i vjerovati svom servisu,' objasnio je Wawrinka. Njegov strateški forhend je donio konačnu pobjedu, čime je postao drugi švicarski muški prvak u Grand Slamu, uz olimpijsko zlato u paru s Federerom iz 2008. 'Olimpijska pobjeda uvijek će biti posebna - moja prva velika pobjeda s dobrim prijateljem za Švicarsku,' rekao je Wawrinka. 'Ali ovaj Grand Slam naslov... to je nešto nezaboravno.'

article_content: A young model's life changed dramatically when an assault left her with permanent facial scarring. Lasha Horton, 23, required extensive medical treatment including 30 stitches after an alleged attacker forced her head through a window at her Nottingham residence in the early hours of October 26, 2012. Plastic surgeons worked for two days to address injuries stretching from her left ear to eye socket, warning that her mixed-race complexion might complicate scar reduction efforts. The incident has jeopardized Horton's £15,000-per-year modeling career, including planned music video appearances and a contract with London agency Demus Castings. Agency director Nicholas Demus confirmed canceled bookings with Flavour fashion magazine and other clients, noting the industry's emphasis on physical appearance. Horton expressed concerns about losing both income and charitable work opportunities, though she hopes to redirect her experiences into advocacy. Nottinghamshire Police reported responding to the 1:50am incident and charging a woman with intentional bodily harm. While legal proceedings continue, Horton remains housebound, grappling with the attack's lasting physical and emotional impacts.

Plastični kirurzi dva dana su radili na ozljedama koje se protežu od lijevog uha do očnog ugla, upozorivši da bi njezin mješoviti etnički porijeklo moglo otežati uklanjanje ožiljaka. Policija Nottinghamshirea izvijestila je o intervenciji u 1:50 ujutro i podignula optužnicu za namjerno nanošenje teških tjelesnih ozljeda. Dok se pravni postupak nastavlja, Horton se suočava s trajnim fizičkim i emocionalnim posljedicama napada, ograničavajući svoje izlaske iz kuće.

article_content: Sanaa, Yemen (CNN) – A Yemeni government warplane crashed north of the capital Wednesday morning, state TV reported. Authorities accused opposition groups of shooting down the aircraft during a military operation. The incident occurred amid ongoing anti-government protests drawing large crowds. Multiple eyewitnesses told CNN that opposition tribes downed the plane as it bombarded a residential area in Arhab district. 'The government kills our loved ones with their weapons. We must defend ourselves,' said Abdullah al-Shaleef, an Arhab resident engaged in clashes with government forces. Witnesses reported Tuesday night's air raids on Arhab and Nehm districts killed two people and wounded four. The aircraft crashed in Bani Hareth, 7km south of Arhab near Sanaa's outskirts. In a separate incident, Yemen's defense minister survived a suicide bombing attack on his convoy Tuesday. Protests continued Monday with tens of thousands marching in Sanaa. President Ali Abdullah Saleh returned Friday after three months in Saudi Arabia recovering from injuries sustained in a June assassination attempt. The United Nations, European Union, and United States have urged Yemen to cease violence and establish a peaceful transition of power. Journalist Hakim Almasmari contributed to this report.

Više očevidaca je izvijestilo CNN kako su opozicijska plemena oborila avion dok je bombardirao stambeno područje u okrugu Arhab. 'Vlada ubija naše voljene svojim oružjem. Moramo se braniti,' izjavio je Abdullah al-Shaleef, stanovnik Arhaba u sukobu s vladinim snagama. Svjedoci su naveli da su zračni napadi u utorak navečer na područjima Arhab i Nehm uzrokovali smrt dvoje ljudi i ranjavanje četvero. Letjelica se srušila u Bani Harethu, 7 km južno od Arhaba na rubu Sane. U drugom incidentu, jemenski ministar obrane izbjegao je atentat kamikaza na svoj konvoj u utorak. Prosvjedi su nastavljeni u ponedjeljak s desetinama tisuća ljudi na ulicama Sane. Predsjednik Ali Abdullah Saleh vratio se u petak nakon trojmjesečnog liječenja u Saudijskoj Arabiji zbog ozljeda zadobivenih u atentatu u junu. Ujedinjeni narodi, Europska unija i Sjedinjene Države pozvale su Jemen na prekid nasilja i mirnu tranziciju vlasti. Novinar Hakim Almasmari doprinio je izvještaju.

article_content: By Emily Kent Smith Most women are content with their natural noses, while some opt for minor adjustments. Cindy Jackson has taken this further by undergoing three nose operations to maintain fashionable features, recently achieving a hybrid style inspired by Kate Middleton and Angelina Jolie. The 58-year-old cosmetic surgery adviser traveled to Croatia for her latest procedure, citing more affordable surgical fees. She prepared Photoshop mockups combining elements from both celebrities' noses to guide her surgeon. Following her £10,000 third procedure last month, Jackson declared: 'This will be my final nose job.' Her first rhinoplasty at 34 replaced her 'disliked' original nose, followed by a second procedure two years later modeled after Nicole Kidman's profile. After 22 years, she deemed that look 'too Eighties' and sought a more 'timeless' appearance. Jackson reports increasing client requests for Middleton/Jolie-inspired features, noting: 'I have clients repeatedly asking for those specific nose shapes - and I understand the appeal.' The Ohio native, who's undergone 57 procedures costing £67,000 total, has modified nearly every body part except her arms and feet - which she plans to address next. The Mail on Sunday continues advocating for stricter cosmetic industry regulations through its 'Stop Cosmetic Surgery Cowboys' campaign, pushing for standardized surgeon qualifications and restrictions on aggressive marketing tactics. Speaking at a Selfridges Beauty Project event, Jackson cautioned: 'The internet presents highly polished, enticing content that influences people's decisions.'
